NEW DELHI: Bar Council of India chairman Manan Kumar Mishra on Saturday apologised to law students following the council's controversial decision to briefly halt the enrolment of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law's 2026 graduating batch as advocates, Bar and Bench reported.In a letter issued on Independence Day, Mishra said he regretted any words or communication connected to the controversy that may have hurt the feelings of law students."If anything connected with the present controversy, any of my words, or letter, has hurt the feelings of our law students, I sincerely regret and apologise for the same. There should be no hesitation in saying so," the letter reads."An expression of regret is not a matter of prestige or ego. It is simply an acknowledgment that the feelings and concerns of our students matter," he added.The apology comes after the BCI directed all state bar councils not to enrol NALSAR's 2026 graduates as advocates until further orders. The council withdrew the directive within hours following an uproar on social media.The BCI had initially said it was examining allegations regarding a campaign against Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's participation in NALSAR's convocation and had sought a report identifying those responsible.The council later modified its decision to allow the enrolment of the university's 2026 graduates before withdrawing the notification altogether. The revised notification said the "vast majority" of students were innocent and should not be made to suffer for the alleged "misconduct" of a few.The controversy began after around 450 graduating NALSAR students urged the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant as chief guest at its convocation. The students cited his alleged refusal to hear pleas concerning "police brutality" against students who had marched to Parliament on July 20 seeking the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG question paper leak in May.The Supreme Court later expressed "strong disapproval" of the BCI's now-revoked order.A bench headed by CJI Kant, and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said students have the right to protest peacefully and described the episode as a "dialogue" between him and the students."If students are protesting peacefully, who is BCI to take action? It is the right of the students to protest peacefully. It is a dialogue between students and me. No one else has to step in," the CJI said.The Supreme Court also stayed any coercive action against students or faculty by the BCI or state councils."It (the letter) was absolutely uncalled for," the bench added.

World.title: ‘Sharma Ji Ka Beta Toh…’: Why some Indian careers are judged before they are chosen?
World.content:
âWhat do you do?â

Sounds like a simple question. But in India, the answer to this question determines your social status.

Is there any scope?

How much will you earn?

What will people say?

Some careers in India instantly earn respect.

Others invite questions.

So when a young person chooses a career, are they really choosing what they want or are they going for what society considers worth choosing?

What are the top careers in India?

A 2018 Global Education Census by Cambridge International, based on responses from nearly 20,000 teachers and students across the world, including 4,400 teachers and 3,800 students in India, found that medicine and engineering continued to dominate career ambitions.

The survey found that 23% of Indian students wanted to become doctors or dentists, while an equal 23% aspired to become engineers. Another 16% wanted to become software engineers, the highest proportion for this career among all countries surveyed. The findings also showed India's strong interest in scientific careers, with 8% of students saying they wanted to become scientists.

Now, letâs figure out why that is so.





What role do parents & society play?

While some students choose these careers out of genuine interest, others pursue them under pressure from parents and society.

Another 2020 study published in the Int J of Indian Culture and Business Management found that parents, peers and societal expectations significantly influence career choices among Indian youth.

TOI also conducted a survey to understand how society perceives different professions and whether certain careers continue to command greater respect than others.

75 % of respondents selected yes when asked if their relatives ever suggested them a âbetterâ career

Among respondents from sectors including journalism, medicine and PR, we received 100% response in âyesâ, agreeing that society accords greater respect to certain professions, with over 80 % respondents selecting both doctors, and IAS/IPS officers emerging as the most prestigious career choices, in second position was engineering.

Around 74 % of them agreed that often-overlooked professions like nurse, police constable, mechanic, cab driver do not receive the same respect as traditionally prestigious careers in medicine and engineering.

Somdeb Dhar Choudhury, one of the respondents and a PR consultant, said, âI grew up in an environment where engineering was considered the more conventional professional route. Many people in my extended family came from engineering backgrounds, and after Class 12, there was an expectation that I would follow a similar path.â

When asked why he thinks PR receives less social recognition, he said, âIn India, professions such as medicine, engineering and civil services have had a clearly understood social identity for generations.

Families know what those careers involve, there is a visible educational path leading to them, and society has established benchmarks of success around them. PR operates very differently. Much of the work happens behind the scenes.

â

Is it affecting mental health?

When asked if the respondents ever felt pressured to choose a career mainly because of its title or status, half of them responded with yes. More than half chose yes when asked if their relatives ever suggested they choose a particular career.

Rashmi N, former Army public school counselor, while speaking to TOI, says, âPeer comparisons lead to self doubt and career indecisions. Falling behind in academics and comparing grades with peers may also trigger withdrawal from friends, low self esteem and or lack of interest to improve.â

On the other hand psychologists say the pressure to choose a socially accepted career may not always be obvious.

Explaining the same, a Delhi-based psychologist Radhika Goyal said, âwhen motivation is driven mainly by fear, fear of failure, criticism, comparison or disappointing the family, rather than genuine enthusiasm.

A student may perform well but still experience burnout, frustration or disengagement.â

Factors influencing parentsâ decisions

While parents may want the best for their children, itâs important to discuss what drives them to push certain careers over others.

1. Job security

For many Indian parents, a âgoodâ career is still closely associated with stability, authority, financial security and social respect.

Rashmi said that this may be because of job stability and authority.

âAuthority, financial stability & fame are the major factors influencing the perception of any career paths.â

âFor more affluent families, social status, community approval and family reputation can weigh heavily on career choices, while for families with fewer financial resources, immediate income and financial security may take precedence,â she said.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you value more in a career? Social Status Job Satisfaction Financial Security 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

2. Unfinished ambitions leading to societal comparisons

Goyal pointed to an often-overlooked factor: parents projecting their own unfinished ambitions or past experiences onto their children.

âParents may sometimes project their own unfinished ambitions, disappointments or experiences onto their childrenâs career choices, often with good intentions. A parent who could not pursue a particular career may believe they are protecting their child from the difficulties they experienced.â

However, this dynamic appears to be changing among a newer generation of parents.

Savita S, a parent of a 24-year-old daughter working in an HR firm, said, âI believe my children are satisfied with my support.â

When asked about the typical âSharma ji ka betaâ comparison, she said that parents are becoming more mindful of how their children respond to such pressure.

âThis kind of comparison is reducing day by day.â

Now, if youâve had your parentsâ support, overcome societal pressure and chosen a career based on your own dreams, are you truly happy with that choice?

What happens when youth passion meets reality?

1. Paycheck

For some young professionals, the pressure around career choices continues even after entering the workforce, with questions of money, job security and growth becoming important factors in deciding whether to stay or change paths.

Aayushi, a journalist, while sharing her experience said, âI was satisfied with choosing a career outside the conventional mainstream, but was disappointed by the financial returns. I am satisfied in terms of doing something different from the generic league. But in terms of money, way too underwhelmed.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

She also sometimes considered changing her career.

Around 56% of respondents selected Low salary, lack of job security and growth as their main reasons to reject a career.

2. Women face another layer of pressure

A 2025 study published in the

International Journal of Trends and Innovations in Business & Social Sciences

found that women were more likely to change careers because of social expectations, especially after marriage, while men more often cited personal interests and changes in the job market.

The gendered perception of careers can also influence how professions are valued.

3. When your profession needs an explanation

For some professionals, however, the pressure is less about being forced to leave a career and more about constantly having to explain its worth.

Somdeb recalled that this became apparent after he entered the industry. âIf someone says they are a doctor, engineer or lawyer, people immediately understand the profession. In PR, you often have to explain what the job involves before people can understand its value. That lack of familiarity created more pressure for me than any direct opposition to my career choice.â

Perhaps the real measure of progress is that there has been a shift, but still there is a long way to go.

World.title: Food regulator failed to penalise 2,430 firms: CAG
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The food regulator failed to impose Rs 5.60 crore in penalties on 2,430 food businesses that either did not file or delayed filing mandatory annual returns, a CAG audit has found, raising questions over enforcement of basic food safety rules.

An audit of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) Eastern Region office in Kolkata found that 1,018 food businesses did not submit their annual returns, while 1,412 filed them late during 2017-18 to 2022-23.

These returns provide FSSAI with information on the quantities of food products manufactured, handled, imported or exported by licensed food businesses during the year. They have to be submitted by May 31.

Businesses that miss the deadline are liable to pay a penalty of Rs 100 for each day of delay, subject to the prescribed limit.

CAG estimated that Rs 5.60 crore in penalties should have been imposed on the 2,430 businesses. However, the audit found that FSSAI had not imposed the penalties. It also noted that none of the defaulters had their licence suspended or cancelled as of August 2023.

Following the audit, FSSAI said improvement notices had been issued to some defaulting food businesses and that notices would be issued again to all defaulters.





Of the Rs 5.60 crore penalty identified by CAG, Rs 2.27 crore had been recovered, according to the report.

The finding is significant because filing an annual return is a basic requirement for licensed food businesses. The audit has highlighted gaps in FSSAI's monitoring and enforcement of this requirement.

NEW DELHI: AIIMS Rishikesh failed to recover Rs 1.78 crore in dues from a contractor and paid Rs 60.21 lakh in inadmissible nursing and dress allowances to College of Nursing faculty, a CAG audit has found.The institute awarded a three-year parking and traffic management contract in August 2019, with a monthly licence fee of Rs 9.015 lakh plus taxes. The contractor began defaulting from the start, but AIIMS did not act despite repeated payment failures. The contractor made only partial payments for about 2.5 years and left the hospital complex in October 2022 without clearing the dues.CAG said this resulted in Rs 1.78 crore in unrealised dues. AIIMS later initiated legal action and moved to forfeit the contractor's Rs 18 lakh security deposit, though it had not been forfeited as of July 2025.In a separate finding, CAG flagged Rs 60.21 lakh paid between April 2018 and March 2023 as nursing and dress allowances to College of Nursing faculty. The faculty were already receiving academic and resource-learning allowances and, according to the audit, their duties did not involve nursing patients or wearing uniforms.The Ministry subsequently directed 10 AIIMS, including Rishikesh, to discontinue nursing allowance for nursing-college faculty, saying the institutes had complied.

World.title: Doctors pledge two hours a week for free care to poor
World.content:
The programme seeks to reach patients from low-income families, rural areas and urban slums who often delay treatment because of cost or the lack of access to specialists.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In an attempt to bridge gaps in access to specialist healthcare, 27 doctors from across Delhi have pledged two hours of free consultation every week for poor and underprivileged patients under a new volunteer initiative, '2 Ghante Desh Ke Naam'.The campaign brings together specialists from ophthalmology, oncology, orthopaedics, psychiatry, paediatrics, cardiology, gynaecology and general medicine, who will provide consultations free of cost through two hospitals and two clinics, as well as via telemedicine for patients in remote and underserved areas. Organisers said the initiative aims to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent patients from seeking timely medical advice.Unlike a centrally funded programme, the initiative is being run collectively by participating hospitals and clinics, each contributing voluntarily by dedicating doctors' time and infrastructure. Organisers said there is no single funding agency or institution leading the campaign.The programme seeks to reach patients from low-income families, rural areas and urban slums who often delay treatment because of cost or the lack of access to specialists.Besides consultations, doctors will also provide treatment guidance and follow-up advice where required. Patients will be able to register directly with participating specialists through dedicated contact numbers issued by each speciality, following which they will be screened and scheduled for consultations.Organisers said the digital component of the initiative would allow patients from smaller towns and villages to consult specialists without travelling long distances. They are also reaching out to medical associations and healthcare institutions across the country to encourage more doctors to volunteer and expand the initiative beyond Delhi."Many patients lose vision because they cannot access timely eye care. If doctors volunteer even a few hours each week, we can help prevent avoidable blindness among the poor," said Dr Ikeda Lal, senior ophthalmologist and medical director, Delhi Eye Centre.Dr L Tomar, senior orthopaedic surgeon and founder of Tomar Foundation, said, "Access to quality orthopaedic care should not depend on a person's ability to pay. Two hours of voluntary service every week can help reduce avoidable disability and improve quality of life."Highlighting the need for accessible mental healthcare, Dr Deepak Raheja, senior psychiatrist and director, Hope Care India, said, "Mental healthcare remains out of reach for many because of financial and social barriers. We want to ensure that those in need can access professional guidance without worrying about cost."Dr Ashish Gupta, chief of medical oncology at Amerix Multispecialty Hospital, said, "Cancer patients often delay treatment because of fear and financial constraints. Making specialist consultations free can encourage earlier diagnosis and timely treatment."

World.title: 'Risk of seizures': Docs flag concerns over Jharkhand student leader Mahto's health
World.content:
Devendra Mahto at Ranchi Sadar Hospital

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mehto is suffering from an electrolyte imbalance, doctors at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi said on Saturday, expressing concern over the health condition of the student leader, who has been on a hunger strike for 15 days.While briefing about Mahto's health, Dr Amrita said that his sodium level had dropped to 124 and ketone bodies had been detected in his urine, indicating starvation.The doctor said that Mahto had refused to take fluids, although he continued to drink water."First, there is Devendra Nath Mahto, who has not eaten for 15 days. He is refusing to take fluids, though he is drinking water. An electrolyte imbalance has been detected in him. Reports show his sodium level is 124, and ketone bodies are present in his urine, indicating starvation," Dr Amrita said.Addressing the press conference, she also shared the health condition of other hunger strikers admitted to the hospital."Next is Umme Habiba. Ketone bodies have been found in her urine as well. Her blood pressure is being maintained due to fluid transfusions. Then there is Rahul Kranti. Ketone bodies have been found in his urine too, at a '3+' level, and his blood pressure is currently being maintained solely through fluid transfusions," she said.This comes after Mahto alleged that police repeatedly "jostled and stopped" him from participating in a Tiranga Yatra at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi.In a post on X, Mahto said, "The police repeatedly jostled and stopped me. Eventually, I sat down right outside the door of my room. I will remain seated here until I am allowed to leave. I will not undergo medical treatment either.""I will stay right here and voice my position. My fight is for the rights of the people and for justice. My voice cannot be suppressed by stopping me," he added.Responding to the allegations, Sadar Hospital Deputy Superintendent Dr Bimlesh Kumar also reiterated concerns over Mahto's health and said that doctors had advised Mahto against seeking discharge and urged him to remain at the hospital for necessary treatment."The situation right now involves a significant electrolyte imbalance; sodium is at 124, and potassium is also low. If the patient exerts themselves in this condition, there is a risk of seizures or similar complications. Under these circumstances, we simply cannot discharge the patient," Dr Kumar said."That is why we have advised against discharge, and we believe he should understand this; discharging him now would lead to serious problems. For the time being, we have advised him to stay here and allow the necessary medical treatment to proceed... his condition does not permit us to let them leave or discharge him. Given the clear signs and symptoms of starvation, we simply cannot discharge the patient in this condition under any circumstances," he added.Thousands of students and aspirants are protesting over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

World.title: Evening news wrap: PM's big shout-outs to Gen Z on I-day; multiple earthquakes jolt Indonesia and more
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced AI training for one crore youth, free online coaching for competitive exams and a nationwide sports talent hunt, linking young Indians directly with the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.

A 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck northern Sumatra hours after a 7.7-magnitude quake hit eastern Indonesia, killing at least 38 people, triggering landslides, power outages, evacuations and ongoing rescue operations.

World.content:

World.title: Even as government considers MDR charge on UPI, data shows cash usage quickening in economy
World.content:
At a time when the government is proposing to allow the levy of a charge on UPI transactions, an analysis shows that the growth in the value of UPI transactions has been slowing for the last five years, while the growth of cash with the public has been quickening over this period.

Paywall: On a charge on UPI transactions

While slowing, the growth of UPI transactions remains faster than the growth of cash among the public, but this margin is shrinking. Experts say this is both a sign of higher economic activity and higher price levels than are being reflected in the official inflation data.

UPI and RuPay debit card transactions are currently free, like cash transactions. However, the government passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 in the recently-concluded Monsoon session of Parliament, which enables it to allow a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charge to be levied on these electronic transactions.

Cash is back

An analysis by The Hindu of data from the Reserve Bank of India shows that the growth rate of cash with the public reached a recent high of about 17% in the COVID-19 pandemic year of 2020-21. Thereafter, the growth of cash with the public fell consistently until 2023-24, where it hit about 4%.

Cash with the public is the total cash in circulation minus what is sitting in banks.

Since then, the growth of cash with the public has been quickening. That is, this growth rate rose to 6.5% in 2024-25 and further to 12% in 2025-26. In 2026-27, cash with the public, at ₹41.8 lakh crore as of July 31, 2026, was nearly 13% higher than in the same period of the previous year.

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and the Payments Corporation of India have made assurances that the general public would not have to pay the MDR charge on UPI transactions and that it would only be levied on certain high value merchants and transactions.

However, the Opposition has said that the merchants who do have to pay this charge would pass that higher cost onto their customers in the form of higher prices and that this could push people back to using cash.

UPI slowing but high

UPI transactions, on the other hand, have seen their growth slowing over the last few years, as per data with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). The value of UPI transactions conducted in the country grew 133% in 2019-20, which then slowed to a relatively robust 95% in 2020-21 as the economy locked down.

It then quickened again to 105% in 2021-22 as the economy opened up and pent-up demand combined with health fears over handling cash to push up UPI usage.

Since then, however, the growth in the value of transactions done on the UPI platform has consistently been slowing, with growth hitting 20.3% in 2025-26. In 2026-27, this has further slowed to 18.7% as of August 2026, as compared to the April-August period of last year.

However, this 18.7% growth in UPI transactions is still higher than the 13% growth in cash with the public in the same period.

Inflation likely understated

According to Pronab Sen, former Chief Statistician of India and former Chairman of the Standing Committee on Statistics, the fact that both cash and UPI are growing should be showing itself in the form of higher inflation rates than what the official numbers are currently showing.

“This would imply that we are undercounting inflation, because that’s where this should show up,” Mr. Sen told The Hindu. “If there is more money being transacted, both digitally and in cash, then that should show up in inflation. The first effect would be there.”

“A lot of this could be explained if the official data showed prices were rising faster than they are,” he added.

The latest official retail inflation data for July 2026 stood at 4.45%, slightly higher than in June, while the wholesale data showed inflation had slowed marginally to 9.8% in July from 9.9% in June.

Signs of robust economy

D.K. Srivastava, chief policy advisor at EY India, says that simultaneous cash and UPI growth is a sign of a vibrant economy.

“The first reason is increasing economic activity in general,” Mr. Srivastava said. “That is to say, high growth rates. We have been maintaining a real growth rate in excess of 7% in the post-COVID years. That is the main reason why both cash transactions and digital transactions have increased.”

Mr. Sen, however, warned that an increase in cash transactions could also point towards distress in the economy brought on by high unemployment, especially among the youth.

World.title: PM’s I-Day speech — Reforms, AI skilling for youth, free online coaching and a warning on ‘dimagi Naxal’
World.content:
Addressing the nation from the ramparts of Red Fort on its 80th Independence Day, just days after massive youth protests rocked the capital, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s speech included a seven-point economic reform plan and an outreach to Gen Z youth, promising AI skilling programmes and free online coaching in an attempt to address post-globalisation anxieties. He also warned the country about the threat of “dimagi Naxals” — intellectual or ideological Naxals — in society, even after the eradication of armed left wing extremism.

At the first Independence Day that saw Vande Mataram preceding the national anthem, the Prime Minister directly addressed challenges facing the youth, from employment worries to the incursion of of Artificial Intelligence in everyday life.

Independence Day LIVE updates

More than one crore youth will be provided AI skills in a “mission mode” drive over the coming year, he said. India’s digital public infrastructure will be used to provide free online coaching to students wishing to take various competitive exams, and there will be a nationwide sports talent hunt among children between five and 15 years of age ahead of the 2036 Olympic Games, he added.

Mr. Modi recalled that, when he had first promoted his ‘Make in India’ initiative, advocates of globalisation had reacted as though it was heresy. In the current global economy, however, every country is thinking for itself, he pointed out.

‘Identify, isolate intellectual Naxals’

This acknowledgement of GenZ anxieties that spilled over into the recent Jantar Mantar protests was, however, spiked by a warning about “intellectual Naxals”.

“For years, people with a Maoist ideology had established themselves in the corridors of power and influenced policymaking, including as advisors on government committees. We have succeeded in eliminating armed Naxalites from the forests and freeing the country from that grave threat, but these ideological Naxalites are waiting for opportunities,” Mr. Modi said. “They are trying to revive the paths of violence and anarchy, and are making various attempts to drag society in the wrong direction. We must identify these ideological Naxalites and isolate them. At the same time, we must connect the country’s young generation with the mainstream effort to build a developed nation,” he added.

Freedom’s Progress Through the Years

He announced a full review and restructuring of civil defence infrastructure. “The nature of warfare is changing. There is no guarantee that wars will now be fought only along the borders,” the Prime Minister said. “A new form of warfare is emerging... Attacks can target a refinery, the banking sector, or a data centre. Infrastructure can be destroyed and factories can be targeted. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra, [a multi-layered defence infrastructure system, with AI and cybersecurity components] last year, and work on it is going on rapidly,” he added.

“The nature of warfare is changing. There is no guarantee that wars will now be fought only along the borders. A new form of warfare is emerging... attacks can target a refinery, the banking sector or a data centre. Infrastructure can be destroyed and factories can be targeted. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra (a multi-layered defence infrastructure with AI and cybersecurity components) last year (2025), and work on it is going on rapidly,” the PM said. A full review and restructuring of the way the civil defence infrastructure functioned would be undertaken, he also announced.

Economic reforms

A large part of the Prime Minister’s speech was devoted to what he termed ‘Saptadhara’ or the seven economic streams where his government was committed to reforms for growth. This includes manufacturing power with emphasis on quality; agriculture and food processing; technology and innovation as evidenced by the opening of the private sector for space exploration, and operationalisation of seven or eight semiconductor plants in the next year or two; the PM GatiShakti plan for multi-modal connectivity; enhanced domestic capabilities in armament production; a green and blue economy, with a coastline changed for full utilisation and increased energy storage; and the projection of India’s soft power, including via yoga, tourism, and animation.

The government has targeted the creation of 100 GW of nuclear energy capacity by 2047, Mr. Modi said, adding that five new reactors will be made operational in the next six to seven years.

Mr. Modi praised the government’s handling of the economy through several global crises. “After beating the COVID-19 pandemic, there was conflict and war everywhere. People had begun fearmongering. Many said there would be no vaccines, no one would be saved. They said no one would get fuel, diesel, fertilizer; people spread all kinds of rumours, and some people derived pleasure in this fearmongering,” he said. “However, despite these challenges, we have followed the spirit of ‘Nagrik Devo Bhava’ (the citizen is equivalent to God), and our preparations have helped us,” he added.

World.title: Engineers in Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department complain over lack of promotion opportunities
World.content:
The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj (RD&PR) Department, despite having been allocated ₹39,609 crore in the recent Budget of the State government, has fewer engineers compared to other engineering departments with lower budgetary outlay, according to the Tamil Nadu Rural Development Engineers Association.

Compared to the position of the RD&PR Department, where there are two Chief Engineers (CE) and three Superintending Engineers (SE), the Water Resources Department, with an allocation of ₹9,264 crore, has 15 CEs and 39 SEs and the Highways and Minor Ports Department (₹21,524 crore) has 10 CEs and 35 SEs, the Association contended.

The body, which recently submitted a representation to the authorities concerned about the lack of opportunities for promotion of engineers in the department, has called for the establishment of district-level quality control laboratories in the department on the lines of those in the Highways and Minor Ports Department. This has become a necessity in view of over 100 civil works and road projects taking place across panchayat unions in the State.

The Association has complained that due to the failure to create sufficient posts in the department, Assistant Engineers, numbering around 450, “have been forced to work in the same position for over 15 years without any promotion.” It has called for the creation of 200 posts for Assistant Engineers; 100 Assistant Executive Engineers; 50 Executive Engineers; 15 SEs; and five CEs.

World.title: ‘Attempt to stigmatise dissent’: Opposition hits out at PM Modi over ‘dimagi Naxal’ jibe
World.content:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday (August 15, 2026) said that people raising their voices for their rights were not anti-national and extended the party’s support to peaceful protests by Gen Z, as the Opposition criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his "dimagi Naxals" remark.

Addressing the Independence Day function at the All India Congress Committee headquarters, Mr. Kharge said attempts to label those questioning the government as anti-national were contrary to the values for which the freedom struggle was fought. “Gen Z, which raises its voice for its rights, is not anti-national," he said, adding that the Congress would stand with movements concerning people’s rights.

Multiple Opposition parties objected to Mr. Modi’s use of the term “dimagi Naxals” (intellectually Naxals) in his Independence Day address, alleging that it was an attempt to stigmatise dissent and intimidate those questioning the government. They also criticised his appeal for political parties to help implement 33% reservation for women in legislatures, alleging that the government had itself kept the quota in abeyance by linking it to delimitation.

Also read: Independence Day LIVE updates

Mr. Kharge said Independence meant freedom not merely from foreign rule but from poverty, discrimination, untouchability, unemployment, injustice and fear. He credited successive Congress governments with building institutions and introducing rights-based legislation, including the right to information, education, food and work. He accused the Modi government of taking credit for the work of earlier governments and said the “real celebration of independence” would come when the poor were heard, young people could fulfil their dreams and no one feared speaking truth to power.

He also attacked the government over the treatment of protesting students, parliamentary accountability and the alleged theft of donations made to the Ram temple in Ayodhya. He said questions over gold, silver and other offerings at the temple should be answered and those responsible for any theft brought to book. Mr. Kharge also alleged government interference in institutions such as the judiciary, Election Commission, universities and investigative agencies.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Mr. Modi had first described his opponents as “urban Naxals” and was now calling them “dimagi Naxals”, terming it a “sure sign of his desperation”. Mr. Ramesh also termed the Prime Minister’s pitch for women’s reservation “dishonest”, pointing out that the legislation passed in 2023 was not implemented in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

Congress president Mr. Kharge alleged that the Prime Minister was claiming credit for all that the Congress has done and warned that “he may bring the national flag down one day”. He also accused the Prime Minister of speaking lies from the Red Fort, as he targeted him on the issues of Ram temple donations “theft” and police action against students.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the Prime Minister first attacked his opponents as “urban Naxals” and is now calling them “dimaagi Naxals”.

Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav urged the government to implement women’s reservation in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. “The Red Fort is not a place from where one should speak lies,” he said.

CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby called the “dimagi Naxal” charge an “atrocious allegation”.

“This is a very convenient accusation that they are Maoists in their mind,” he said. He added that women’s reservation should be implemented in existing seats rather than being linked to delimitation.

Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav said the Red Fort is not the place from where one should speak lies, and urged the Centre to implement the Women Reservation Bill in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

CPI(M) General Secretary M. A. Baby said, “They always wanted to accuse people in the Opposition that they are anti-national. This is a very convenient accusation that they are Maoist in their mind. It is an atrocious allegation.” On women’s reservation, he said all political parties should press the government to implement the quota in the existing seats, instead of linking it to delimitation.

CPI general secretary D. Raja said Mr. Modi had chosen to target dissenters even on Independence Day. “This is nothing but an attempt to stigmatise dissent and intimidate those who question the government,” he said, asking the Prime Minister to answer questions from students and young people on education and employment.

World.title: PM Modi's I-Day speech will be a milestone towards Viksit Bharat journey: Amit Shah
World.content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday (August 15, 2026) said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Independence Day address was imbued with the resolve for Swadeshi and prosperity and added that it will prove to be a milestone in the journey towards becoming a leading nation across all sectors.

In a post on X, Mr. Shah said Mr. Modi outlined a comprehensive roadmap to build a ‘Viksit Bharat’ driven by the spirit of ‘nation first’, ‘drug-free’ and a ‘safe India’.

He also said the Prime Minister highlighted the unprecedented progress made over the last 12 years in sectors such as semiconductors, critical minerals, energy, and railway transport.

He presented the mantra of Saptadhara — seven pillars of strength — to propel the country to new heights and achieve self-reliance across all sectors, Mr. Shah said.

“To channel the potential of the youth, Modi Ji announced initiatives to provide AI skilling to over one crore young people in a single year, establish a network for free online coaching, and launch a talent hunt campaign for the 2036 Olympics,” Mr. Shah said on ‘X’.

Ambitious targets

The Prime Minister set ambitious targets, such as achieving 100 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity and establishing eight new semiconductor units by 2047, he said.

In another post, Mr. Shah said the spirited rallying cry of the freedom movement — Vande Mataram — was sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time today, 80 years after Independence.

“Witnessing this historic moment not only gave me goosebumps but filled my entire being with sheer ecstasy,” he said.

World.title: HC CJ appeal to legal fraternity
World.content:
Chief Justice of Telangana High Court Aparesh Kumar on Saturday exhorted the legal fraternity to remember the suggestion of Mahatma Gandhi to think about the last person in the queue before taking a decision.

Addressing the gathering of judges, advocates, staff and others after hoisting the national flag on the HC premises on Independence Day, the CJ said that nearly 14.13 crore pages of the High Court records and 8.89 crore pages of district judicial records had been scanned and digitised so far. The precious year, 90,357 cases were instituted while 80,020 cases were disposed of in the HC, he said.

This had translated into 88.5% of disposal rate. The construction of zone-II in the proposed new HC complex at Rajendranagar was in progress. Nearly, 25% of the works were completed. The works relating to Cultural Centre being built at the HC guest house at Ashok Vihar has reached the final stage. The State government had allocated ₹751.45 crore for building court buildings, residences for judicial officers and staff for the financial year 2026-27, the CJ said.

World.title: MSMEs in Coimbatore to explore green hydrogen sector
World.content:
The Micro, Small and Medium-scale industries (MSMEs) in Coimbatore district will explore with Japanese collaboration opportunities in green hydrogen sector.

P. Ponram, vice-president of the Coimbatore District Small Industries Association, told The Hindu that the association has held talks with H2 Innovation that is looking for partners in Tamil Nadu for manufacture and market of green hydrogen fuel cells. “We will visit Japan in October and continue our discussions,” he said.

Green hydrogen is a promising sector that the MSMEs can benefit from as producers and consumers. India already has green hydrogen buses. Hence, the association will see how the MSMEs can be involved in this sector, he said.

Karunanidhi Kasinathan, founder and chairman of K-KCCS India Private Limited (an Indo-Japan bridge organisation), told The Hindu that KCCS in association with H2 Innovation Co. Ltd., Japan, is facilitating a series of initiatives to promote collaboration between Japanese technology companies, Indian industries, and educational institutions in green hydrogen, renewable energy, and decarbonisation.

“We are signing tri-partite Memoranda of Understanding with five educational institutions in Tamil Nadu to promote research in green hydrogen and make it cost competitive for the Indian market,” he said.

With high labour and land costs, Japan is looking at technology transfer to expand quickly production of green hydrogen fuel cells. “We are looking for industry partners to take to manufacture and take to market the green hydrogen fuel cells,” he said.

Yosuke Mori, Representative Director of H2 Innovation, added that the capacity can range from 100 KW to 1 MW. “We have done 150 installations in Japan of varying capacity from 500 watts to 50 KW each. We are in discussion with investors in India,” he said.

Initially, about 30 % of the fuel cell can be made in India and the special cylinders will come from Japan. When the manufacturing eco system develops in India the entire cell can be made here, he said.

The minimum investment required to set up a plant here will be ₹20 crore to ₹25 crore. Customers who are mandated to use green hydrogen by the Indian government will be targeted customers initially. . The Union government is mandating all data centres to be powered by renewable energy. For them these fuel cells will be an ideal option and the large data centre investors will not mind spending higher amount to go for clean energy. There are plans to hold talks in all the southern States for this project, he said.

World.title: Devendra Mahto alleges assault by Ranchi police after being stopped from joining Tiranga Yatra
World.content:
Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been undergoing treatment at Ranchi Sadar Hospital, has slammed the police for stopping him when he tried to take part in the Tiranga Yatra organised by the protesting students on the occasion of 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.

Mr. Mahto, who is leading the faction of JPSC-JSSC Nyay Manch, has been on a hunger strike for the past 14 days in support of the demands raised by the students over alleged irregularities in the recruitment examination in Jharkhand.

Also Read :Independence Day LIVE updates

When the police did not allow him to leave the room where he was admitted, an altercation took place between police personnel and Mr. Mahto. The JLKM leader alleged that he sustained an injury to his chest while being stopped and jostled by the police. Mr. Mahto also alleged that the police assaulted and beat up his associates who came to rescue him.

He also shared the footage of the altercation on his official social media account.

VIDEO | Ranchi: Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for the past 14 days over the alleged recruitment exam irregularities in Jharkhand, claims police are not allowing him to attend the Tiranga Yatra.



(Source: Third Party) pic.twitter.com/4MsYf7PBkM — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) August 15, 2026

“For 14 days, I have been on a hunger strike, and today the police tried to push and forcefully stop me along with my companions. The police also assaulted my people who were with me. Despite being hungry for several days, I stand firm for my rights and the voice of the people. They cannot silence our voice by stopping us in this manner,” Mr. Mahto wrote on X.

Police action ‘raises serious questions’

He further said, “Despite being on a hunger strike for 14 days, the way the entire police force came down aggressively just for expressing a desire to hoist the national flag and participate in the Tiranga Yatra raises several serious questions on this day of Independence. During this time, my people were also brutally beaten and thrashed to the ground. Is this the free India we gained from the sacrifices of Lord Birsa Munda and Bhagat Singh? Is this the form of India that Subhas Chandra Bose, Khudiram Bose, Chandrashekhar Azad, Mahatma Gandhi, and Baba Saheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar dreamed of?”

After the alleged assault, Mr. Mahto, along with his people, sat down on dharna right outside his room.

“Until I am allowed to leave from here, I will keep sitting right here. I will not even get my treatment done, and I will stay here to raise my concern. My fight is for the rights of the people and for justice. They (Police) cannot silence my voice by stopping me,”Mr. Mahto said.

Later, he spoke to his party supremo and MLA Tiger Jairam Mahto over a video call and narrated his ordeal, how he was stopped by the police and allegedly assaulted.

“The answer will be sought from the government on the floor of the House. On the 80th Independence Day in free India, why was a protester, who has been on a hunger strike for 14 days, prevented from hoisting the flag? Why was he stopped from joining the Tiranga Yatra? And why is he not being given the freedom to seek treatment as per his own wish? The answer to all these questions will be sought from the government on the floor of the house,” Mr. Mahto said in the post later in the day.

Mr. Mahto was highlighted earlier when educationist Sonam Wangchuk spoke to him over a video call and urged him to end his fast on August 5, 2026. Also, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke had spoken to him over a video call, inquiring about the protest.

Repeated attempts to contact Ranchi Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Rakesh Ranjan and Ranchi City SP Paras Rana proved futile.

World.title: Political rivals should not let differences turn into animosity, says Nawaz
World.content:
PML-N supremo and former prime minister Nawaz Sharif said on Saturday that while political differences between opponents were common during elections, they should never turn into animosity, apparently referring to the deepening differences between the ruling party and its coalition partner, the PPP, at the Centre.

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities that have been ongoing for over two months.

Addressing a party convention in Murree, the party president congratulated the winners of the elections in AJK, while extending commiserations to the losing candidates. However, he noted that the complaints from the PPP have been “upsetting”.

“We have always maintained good relations with our opponents. There is always disagreement in politics, but it should not reach the point where it creates animosity,” he said. “This is unacceptable.”

The PML-N supremo noted that AJK’s atmosphere has always been good, but lamented seeing the buildup of enmity.

“I was upset over their losses, and I have good relations with them personally,” Nawaz said. “We need to look at those factors that contributed to their defeat. We had very good candidates who bravely contested these elections. If they were defeated, we must look at the reasons why.”

He noted, “We can lose seats, but we cannot lose our spirit”.

“God has granted us victory in these conditions. As you know, there have been three phases in these elections; the third phase has yet to conclude. But God granted us a majority in the first two phases. We cannot thank Him enough,” Nawaz added, warning that there is “no room” for hurting public sentiment.

The PML-N supremo opined that this is the first time that such an environment was created in AJK. He attributed it to successive governments failing to fulfil their duties and meet the needs and requests of the people, regardless of which ever party was in power.

“We absolutely need to enable progress in AJK, whatever way we can. We need to resolve problems there, and we will do what we’ve done in Punjab there,” Nawaz stressed.

“It should be our duty, and we need to fulfil public sentiment. If, God forbid, we fail to deliver, the people of AJK will grow angry, and the reason behind it is valid. We would then need to look inward.”

The PML-N supremo noted that the region needs a great deal of development and tasked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to provide AJK with as much funding as possible to build roads, hospitals, and ensure people have livelihoods.

“Tourism needs to be promoted, and industry must be established. Agriculture requires our full attention, and [we can provide] agricultural loans like those in Punjab,” he added.

Moreover, he said that people in Punjab are receiving loans for their houses and expressed his intention to launch such schemes in AJK.

“I will absolutely direct Shehbaz sahib to launch these schemes in this region, and besides that, provide funding,” Nawaz declared.

“People [need to] feel that they are being granted their rights. The people of AJK look at Punjab’s roads, hospitals and hope they are built in AJK; AJK’s children want laptops in their hands, and people should receive Kisaan cards and livelihoods.”

Nawaz further said that the rest of Pakistan was moving forward and was different from the past, while hailing Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s efforts and vowing that the current problems would be resolved very soon.

“Punjab is changing, and AJK should be changed in the same way,” he emphasised.

PPP should ‘consider the logic’ of claiming polls were rigged: CM Maryam

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif spoke about the PPP’s allegations of electoral rigging in the AJK polls, saying that it should “consider the logic” of making such claims.

“It is upsetting that they (PPP) made false allegations of rigging against the PML-N. When they won in Gilgit-Baltistan, they made no claims of rigging; where they lost, they made these allegations,” she told the party conference.

She added that the PPP could not promise the people of AJK new roads and a clean atmosphere, as they were unable to provide those to the people of Sindh.

“In making these allegations, they forgot that the government, administration, president, prime minister and staff were theirs. They should consider logic when levelling allegations against others,” she added.

The polls and allegations of rigging

The polls are being held in phases amid unrest in the region.

The PML-N bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur division in the first phase on July 27 and 15 in the second phase on Aug 2 , comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The PPP, on the other hand, won only 10 constituencies during these phases.

The third phase, held on Monday, was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

Elections in 23 polling stations of the two constituencies, which had been postponed earlier, were held today.

The PPP has criticised the conduct of the AJK elections, with a high-level meeting of the party in Islamabad terming the polls “rigged and violent” and expressing serious concern over the role of the AJK Election Commission.

Earlier this week, a meeting chaired by PPP Women’s Wing president and AJK affairs in-charge Faryal Talpur, also criticised the phase-wise conduct of the elections and demanded the immediate completion of polling in the remaining two districts of the third phase and seven constituencies of Poonch so that the Legislative Assembly could be fully constituted.

The participants raised questions over the suspension of internet services, shortages of polling material and staff at some polling stations, and alleged inadequate security arrangements.

World.title: AJK elections: PPP, PML-N candidates retain lead in Bagh after repolling
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Sardar Ziaul Qamar of the PPP and Sardar Mir Akbar of the PML-N retained the lead in their respective constituencies in Bagh, after results were received from all 23 polling stations where repolling was held on Saturday.

According to unofficial and unverified results, Qamar defeated the PML-N’s Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas in LA-15 (Central Bagh) by 1,891 votes. He secured 17,118 votes against Minhas’s 15,227. Repolling was held at nine polling stations in the constituency.

It was the third consecutive defeat for Minhas in the constituency, who had entered electoral politics in 2016 under the banner of the PML-N, won that election and served as a minister during the following five years.

Qamar, meanwhile, secured his second consecutive victory after winning the 2023 by-election.

In LA-16 (Eastern Bagh), the PML-N’s Akbar defeated the PPP’s Sardar Qamaruz Zaman by 3,833 votes, securing 20,796 votes against his rival’s 16,963. Repolling was held at 14 polling stations in the constituency.

Akbar has won four elections previously, making Saturday’s victory his fifth overall and third consecutive win.

According to local journalists, Akbar’s sustained presence in his constituency, where he regularly attends celebrations, is believed to have contributed to his popularity. Constituents said he was known for attending even occasions marking the death of villagers’ livestock.

Turnout remained low in both constituencies, according to witnesses, with voters at some polling stations “voluntarily” opting not to cast their ballots.

Polling was, however, held peacefully, with adequate security arrangements for polling staff and voters. Polling officials described the conduct of voters towards them and security personnel as cordial.

“Though no voters showed up [at some polling stations], the attitude and cooperation of local notables with polling staff and security forces was exemplary, including arrangements for their accommodation and meals,” said a presiding officer in LA-15.

The repolling results took the PML-N’s tally to 25 seats and the PPP’s to 12 in the AJK Legislative Assembly. Sajid Iqbal Abbasi, who won LA-14 (Dhirkot) against Muslim Conference president and former AJK premier Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan by a large margin, also reportedly decided to support the PML-N.

Monday results

In the third phase of polling on Monday, PPP’s Qamar secured 16,637 votes in LA-15 (Bagh Central), followed by PML-N’s Minhas with 15,015 and Jamaat-i-Islami’s retired Brig Dr Muhammad Khan with 12,259. But as polling could not be held at nine stations in the constituency, the commission withheld the result.

Similarly, the result of LA-16 (Eastern Bagh) was also withheld after polling could not be held at 14 stations, which have a combined 7,238 registered voters.

Results from the remaining polling stations showed that PML-N’s Akbar, who secured 19,515 votes, was leading his closest rival, PPP’s Zaman, by 3,225 votes.

In both constituencies, all five candidates had accused their opponents of rigging.

Rathore notified as returned candidate from LA-17

Meanwhile, the AJK Election Commission notified AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore as the returned candidate from LA-17. The notification was issued late on Friday and was provided to the media on Saturday.

LA-17 (Haveli), where Rathore was contesting from, emerged as the most contentious constituency during the third phase of the polls on Monday. The election was thrown into fresh controversy on Wednesday after the returning officer issued the Form 27 declaring him the winner despite an assurance, according to his PML-N rival Engr Mohsin Aziz, that the result would not be announced until his complaint was taken up by the Election Commission.

Aziz subsequently challenged the election, with the AJK Chief Election Co­­mmissioner (CEC) retired Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on Thursday reserving his decision after hearing arguments from both sides.

On Saturday, the Election Commission said that it would announce the verdict on the petitions at 5pm.

AJK polls

The PML-N bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur division in the first phase on July 27 and 15 in the second phase on Aug 2 comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The PPP, on the other hand, won only 10 constituencies during these phases.

The polls are being held in phases amid unrest in the region.

The third phase, held on Monday, was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

On Monday, polls went ahead in Bagh and Haveli, but the Election Commission later withheld the results of two constituencies pending repolling at 23 polling stations.

It announced the result for LA-14 (Bagh-I), commonly known as Dhirkot, where Jammu Kashmir Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sajid Iqbal Abbasi secured a landslide victory with 40,522 votes.

World.title: JI announces countrywide protest against petroleum levy on Sunday
World.content:
LAHORE: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Pakistan Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Saturday announced that the party would stage sit-ins outside the Governor Houses in Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar and the Chief Minister House in Lahore on Sunday against the levy imposed on petroleum products and other taxes.

The sit-ins would begin at 4pm, he said, adding that participants would march from different cities to reach the designated sites.

Addressing a packed press conference at Mansoora alongside the party’s central and provincial office-bearers, Rehman said, “We want to convey the voice of suppressed labourers, students and other sections of society to the government peacefully.”

He warned that if the government tried to create trouble or interfere with the protest, the campaign for lower petrol prices could turn into a movement to topple the government.

The JI emir said the party had organised sit-ins at 510 locations the previous week and that “not a single flowerpot was broken” during the protests. “We will come peacefully and return after securing our right,” he said.

The JI chief said that “we are giving the time for the start of the sit-ins but not for their ending”, adding that the party was demanding that the petrol price be fixed at Rs225 after abolishing the levy, while the price of roti be fixed at Rs10 and those of flour, electricity and gas be reduced.

He also called for cuts in flour, electricity and gas prices and demanded that vehicles used by federal and provincial bureaucrats, judges, ministers, advisers and others should not have engine capacities exceeding 1,300cc.

The JI leader further demanded an end to free electricity, gas, fuel and other “extravagant privileges”, saying the taxes collected from the public should be spent on the people.

He alleged that the government was meeting its expenses at the expense of citizens’ hard-earned money, while the rulers were unwilling to give up their privileges.

“Rs130 is being collected per litre of petrol as extortion in the name of the levy,” he alleged.

Rehman also claimed that federal government expenditure had been estimated at Rs800 billion but had reached Rs1 trillion.

He questioned the government’s priorities, alleging that public transport remained unavailable while the Punjab chief minister was travelling in an aircraft worth Rs11bn.

“If the masses will not come out now, then at what point will they leave their homes?” he asked.

The JI emir said his party had no personal agenda and always raised issues concerning the public. He warned that the party had a “second plan” if the government attempted to stop the protests, saying the sit-ins would then be expanded across the country.

JI Deputy Chiefs Liaqat Baloch, Mian Muhammad Aslam and Dr Attaur Rehman, Acting Secretary General Nazeer Ahmed Janjua, Deputy Secretary Azhar Iqbal Hassan, Lahore Emir Ziauddin Ansari, Central Punjab Secretary Babar Rashid, social media head Salman Sheikh, and JI Youth representatives Ahmad Salman Baloch and Jibran Butt were also present at the press conference.

World.title: Rescuers search for survivors as Indonesian 7.7 quake death toll rises to 47
World.content:
Rescuers combed through debris for survivors on Saturday after a powerful earthquake struck off Indonesia’s eastern Flores island, killing at least 47 people, according to disaster officials.

The national disaster management agency (BNPB) raised the death toll from 40 late on Saturday, while rescue official Fathur Rahman said 50 people were injured in the 7.7-magnitude quake.

Suharyanto, who leads the BNPB, said earlier that people were trapped in several buildings.

“These will be the initial targets of the disaster response teams,” he said.

Nearly 160 houses, dozens of educational and health facilities and other public buildings were damaged when the earthquake struck the popular tourist island in Indonesia’s east, the BNPB reported.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said preparations were underway to bring aid to some 2,000 people in temporary shelters.

The government sent 50,000 aid packages weighing a total of 275 tonnes to the area, and European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen offered help from the bloc’s Copernicus Earth observation satellites.

“Europe stands ready to deploy Copernicus, our eyes in the sky, to support search and rescue efforts. Indonesia, we stand with you,” she wrote on X.

‘Like we were on a trampoline’

“I have never felt an earthquake this big,” Yulian Juita Ekalia, who lives in Ruteng city — more than 100 kilometres west of the epicentre — told AFP by telephone hours after the tremor.

“It felt like we were on a trampoline; it was really scary,” said the 37-year-old university lecturer, who was jolted awake at around 5:30am (2130 GMT on Friday).

“As I rushed to get outside, everything in the house fell down: the television, my son’s trophies, the dish racks, suitcases on top of the wardrobes. When I got outside, my son and neighbours were already there, screaming in fear.”

Rescue official Fathur told AFP the focus was on locating victims who may be buried under rubble, but rescue efforts have been complicated by landslides cutting off roads. Many Flores inhabitants were left without electricity and telecommunications.

Residents in Nagekeo, an area close to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated early Saturday — a possible sign of an approaching tsunami, AFP journalists witnessed.

While a tsunami warning was lifted, authorities urged people not to return to damaged buildings for fear that aftershocks may bring them down.

Hundreds remained outside hours later as dozens of aftershocks shook the island, the strongest measured at a magnitude of 6.1.

Waves of up to 1.6 metres were reported in some coastal regions of Flores, according to Indonesia’s BMKG geological agency.

Fleeing in panic

Yulian said she had dragged her stove outside and was cooking there, fearing further tremors. She said she saw patients being treated under emergency tents outside a nearby hospital.

Nagekeo resident Yohanes Babo, 56, said he was at a market when the earth started shaking in the early morning hours.

“The shaking was strong. Thankfully, we were already outside the house,” he told AFP. “People were panicking, running here and there. We’re evacuating for the time being… and trying to get to the hills.”

The epicentre of the shallow quake was located just off the north coast of the island, US and Indonesian authorities said. The affected areas have few, if any, high-rise buildings.

A second, deep onland quake was measured at a magnitude of 6.9 near Pematangsiantar on Sumatra island — thousands of kilometres away — some 12 hours after the Flores tremor.

There were no initial reports of damage or casualties, and no tsunami alert was issued.

Indonesia experiences frequent earthquakes due to its location in the Pacific “Ring of Fire”, an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.

Flores was struck by a 7.7-magnitude earthquake in 1992, which triggered a tsunami and resulted in around 2,500 deaths.

A devastating 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 struck off the coast of Sumatra and triggered a tsunami that killed 220,000 throughout the region, about 170,000 of them in Indonesia, in one of the deadliest natural disasters in recorded history.

Condolences

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives in the earthquake.

“On behalf of the people of Pakistan, the President extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and expressed solidarity with the Government and people of Indonesia in this difficult hour.”

He further said that Pakistan was ready to extend all possible assistance.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said he was “deeply saddened” by the loss of life and destruction caused by the earthquake.

He extended his heartfelt condolences to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and the people of Indonesia and the bereaved families on behalf of the government and the Pakistani public.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with all those affected, and we pray for the swift recovery of the injured,” he wrote on X. “Pakistan stands shoulder to shoulder with the brotherly people of Indonesia and wishes strength and resilience to all those facing this difficult time.”

World.title: Women exercising lawful rights should not be subjected to violence with impunity: SC
World.content:
While rejecting an appeal by a convict who murdered his former wife just two days after she obtained a judicial decree dissolving their marriage, the Supreme Court on Saturday ruled that women who exercise their lawful rights should not be subjected to violence with impunity.

“This court, being mindful of the constitutional imperative to protect the life and dignity of women and to ensure that those who exercise their lawful rights are not subjected to violence with impunity, finds no basis to interfere with the concurrent conviction,” observed Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar.

Headed by Justice Kakar, a three-judge Supreme Court bench, also comprising Justice Salahuddin Panhwar and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up an appeal against the Lahore High Court’s June 25, 2025, rejection of his plea.

According to the prosecution’s case, petitioner Wasim Abbas on Oct 11, 2020, at approximately 3pm, forcibly entered the home of Irshad Begum in Lahore. Armed with a .30-bore pistol, he was also accompanied by two unidentified accomplices on a motorcycle.

The petitioner entered a room where his former wife, Shehnaz Bibi, and Naeem Bibi were resting on charpoys. After taunting the deceased about her demand for divorce, Abbas fired multiple shots at her, inflicting six firearm wounds to her abdomen, hand, thighs and back. An accomplice fired an additional shot below her right knee. Shehnaz Bibi succumbed to her injuries at the scene.

The SC noted that the motive was a deep-seated resentment stemming from the deceased’s successful suit for dissolution of marriage. An ex parte divorce decree had been passed in her favour on Oct 9, 2020 — merely 48 hours before the murder.

Justice Kakar, writing the judgment, emphasised that the deceased had lawfully exercised her rights under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939, and the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961.

The four-page judgment underscored the constitutional obligation under Articles 9, 14 and 25 of the Constitution to protect the life, dignity and equal treatment of all citizens, including women.

The judgment also cited the 2019 Shazia Perveen case to highlight that a woman who seeks legal dissolution of marriage through the proper judicial process is exercising a fundamental right. Any violence perpetrated against her for exercising such a right strikes at the very heart of the constitutional order and must be met with the full rigour of the law.

Earlier, the trial court had convicted Abbas under Section 302(b) of the PPC, sentencing him to death as ta’zir, along with a direction to pay Rs500,000 in compensation to the legal heirs under Section 544-A of the Cr.P.C.

He was also convicted under Section 449 of the PPC and sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment and fined Rs50,000. All sentences were ordered to run concurrently.

The Supreme Court found the ocular evidence provided by Irshad Begum (PW-8) and Naeem Bibi (PW-9) to be “reliable, trustworthy and confidence-inspiring”. The court noted that, as inmates of the deceased’s parental home, they were natural witnesses to the domestic crime.

The court further highlighted that the incident took place in broad daylight, reducing the possibility of mistaken identity. Abbas was personally known to the witnesses by name and face as the former husband of the deceased.

Additional corroborating evidence included the recovery of the crime weapon on Abbas’s pointation, with a ballistic examination confirming that the empties recovered from the scene matched the seized weapon. Medical evidence also provided strong corroboration of the prosecution’s case.

Rejecting any leniency, the bench observed that “no extenuating or mitigating circumstances” existed to warrant commutation of the death penalty. The court characterised the offence as “exceptionally brutal, calculated, premeditated and cold-blooded”, carried out inside the sanctity of the deceased’s home.

The judgment emphasised that the murder, committed just 48 hours after the judicial decree, demonstrated “ruthless defiance of the law”.

In cases involving deliberate violence against women exercising their legal and marital rights, the court held that “the capital penalty is fully justified to uphold the rule of law and satisfy the ends of justice”.

World.title: KP rejects Centre’s proposal to deduct Rs6.4bn from federal transfers
World.content:
PESHAWAR: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government has rejected a federal proposal for an at-source deduction of Rs6.4 billion from federal transfers payable to the provinces.

Details available with Dawn show that on Aug 5, the Finance Ministry informed the Accountant General of Pakistan Revenues (AGPR) Peshawar office about the proposed at-source deduction.

“I am directed to convey at source deduction of Rs6.4 billion for the month of July 2026, on behalf of government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the letter said.

It said that the amount was adjustable in the accounts for FY 2026-27, requesting a formal advice of adjustment, when carried out, to be provided to the division.

However, on Thursday, KP Finance Department wrote to the Accountant General KP, stating that the KP government had not approved the finance division’s proposed deduction.

“The MoU circulated by the federal government for this purpose has not been approved by the provincial cabinet or signed by the provincial government, nor has any budgetary provision been made for the proposed arrangement in the provincial budget for FY 2026-27. Significantly, the circulated MoU itself provides that no at-source deduction shall be made from the provincial share,” the letter said.

It said the constitutional position was clear and that Article 164 of the Constitution did not authorise unilateral deductions from funds constitutionally payable to a province. It added that no express consent or authorisation under the said article had been granted by the KP government.

“Any deduction from the province’s constitutional fiscal entitlement must have an express constitutional or statutory basis and cannot be effected merely through an executive or accounting instruction,” it said.

The letter further said that the matter was also discussed in the meeting chaired by the advisor to the chief minister on finance, attended by representatives of the AG KP Office, wherein it was decided that no action would be taken without the concurrence of the KP government.

“In view of the above, it is requested that no deduction, debit, adjustment or accounting entry of Rs6.400 billion, or any amount on this account, may be made against the KP government unless expressly concurred with by the provincial government and supported by lawful constitutional/statutory authority,” it said, adding that the AGPR may also be informed accordingly not to record or give effect to any such transaction on behalf of the KP government without its express concurrence.

In a statement, Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said that the federal government, prior to the budget, had demanded additional funds from the KP government, just as it had from other provinces.

CM Afridi said that he had made the provision of this amount conditional upon a meeting with incarcerated PTI leader Imran Khan and his permission.

The second condition was that the merged districts should be given their constitutional and legitimate share under the 11th National Finance Commission, and a period of six months was set for this; otherwise, an ordinance would be issued for the purpose under the 7th National Finance Commission.

However, he said that while their second condition was immediately accepted and formally made part of the proceedings of the National Economic Council meeting, a meeting with Imran was not arranged before the budget.

Afridi said that the KP government had, to date, neither approved nor signed any memorandum of understanding with the federal government regarding the additional amount. Besides, he said that the federal grant was not included in the provincial budget for FY2026-27 either.

CM Afridi added that the KP government had already filed a petition with the Federal Constitutional Court for the enforcement of its constitutional rights under the National Finance Commission.

“My government will not compromise on any of KP’s constitutional, financial, and National Finance Commission rights and the federal government cannot be granted the authority to unilaterally deduct funds from a province’s due financial share on the basis of any memorandum of understanding or arrangement that has not been approved or signed by the provincial government,” he said.

World.title: India's Modi woos youth with free coaching, AI training
World.content:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Saturday his government would provide free online coaching lessons for competitive exams, weeks after massive youth-led protests forced the education minister to resign.

Modi said the initiative was aimed at easing the financial burden on millions of families caught up in the country’s fiercely competitive education system.

The 75-year-old leader made the announcement while speaking from the ramparts of New Delhi’s imposing 17th-century Red Fort to mark the country’s independence from Britain on August 15, 1947.

“We have decided to provide free online coaching for various competitive examinations for our youth. We have the digital public infrastructure, and we have highly talented teachers and educators,” he said.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi waves as he attends the Independence Day celebrations at the historic Red Fort in Delhi, India on August 15, 2026. —Reuters

The move comes after nationwide protests, triggered by the leak of a key medical entrance examination paper and a series of other recruitment scandals, culminated in the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan last month.

The protests exposed deep frustration among young Indians over access to jobs and educational opportunities.

They also highlighted immense pressures on students in India, the world’s most populous nation, where admission to government-run colleges remains one of the most sought-after pathways to economic security.

The cut-throat competition has fuelled a sprawling coaching industry where students spend years preparing, often at enormous financial cost for their families.

Modi said the free online classes would ease financial burden on “poor and middle-class families”.

“The competition surrounding coaching classes has become a huge burden for middle-class families… [Students] can stay close to their families, receive their care, and avoid placing an additional financial burden on them,” he said.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi greets children during the Independence Day celebrations at the historic Red Fort in Delhi, India on August 15, 2026. —Reuters

Modi also announced plans to train several million young people in artificial intelligence tools.

“We have decided in the next one year, one crore (10 million) youth will be given training in AI skills,” he said.

Since the protests, authorities have attempted to appease the nation’s youth, with the parliament hiking penalties for leaking exam papers.

Critics say the protests posed one of the biggest challenges to Modi’s government since coming to power in 2014.

Growth framework

In a speech lasting more than an hour, Modi also reiterated his government’s vow to help India achieve the status of a developed country in the next 20 years, announcing a seven-point growth and reform framework.

The initiative would focus on manufacturing, agriculture, technology and defence, as well as India’s “soft power” through yoga, tourism and handicrafts.

India, Asia’s third-largest economy, must “establish itself as a trusted global supply chain partner for the world”, Modi said of manufacturing.

In the coming years, he said India will have eight more semiconductor chip plants and five nuclear reactors which will generate 100 gigawatts of power by 2047.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi (2L) waves to the members of National Cadet Corps (NCC) after addressing the nation at the Red Fort during the celebrations to mark country’s Independence Day in New Delhi on August 15, 2026. —AFP

Last year, the government allowed private firms to build and operate atomic power projects, underlining a push for alternative energy.

Modi said young people stood to gain the most from his vision for development.

“The youth have a big role to play in the journey towards a developed India… the greatest beneficiary of a developed India is the youth of the country.”

World.title: Aleem Khan expresses support for Hazara province, calls for new administrative units
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) President Abdul Aleem Khan on Saturday expressed support for the creation of Hazara province in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying people across the country wanted new provinces to be created on administrative grounds.
